seoTitle: Free GPT Token Counter for GPT-4 and GPT-4o
metaDescription: Count tokens in text with the exact cl100k_base and o200k_base encodings side by side, plus chat message overhead. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Counts tokens for your text under both OpenAI encodings at once. A second box accepts chat messages as JSON and adds the usual per-message overhead to estimate a request size.
why:
Prompts have a budget. Context windows, rate limits and per-token pricing all depend on counts, and guessing from word counts is off by a wide margin for code, numbers and non-English text.

Paste your text and see the exact figure for cl100k_base, used by GPT-4 and GPT-3.5, and for o200k_base, used by GPT-4o and later models. If you are building a chat request, paste the messages as a JSON array and the tool adds the per-message overhead from OpenAI's cookbook rule: three tokens per message, one more for a name and three to prime the reply. That total is an estimate, since real usage can vary slightly by model. All counting is local in your browser.
howTo: Paste the text you want to count into the Text box.
Optionally paste chat messages as a JSON array of role, optional name and content.
Read the token counts for cl100k_base and o200k_base.
Use the chat total, with its content-only and overhead split, to plan your request size.

faq.a: Each message adds 3 tokens, plus 1 if it has a name, plus the tokens of every field value, and 3 more tokens are added once for the reply. It is the cookbook approximation, not a guarantee for every model version.

faq.q: What is the difference between the two encodings?
faq.a: cl100k_base belongs to GPT-4 and GPT-3.5-turbo, o200k_base to GPT-4o and later families. The newer one has a larger vocabulary and usually produces fewer tokens for non-English text and code.

faq.q: Will it count tool calls or images?
faq.a: No. Function and tool definitions, images, audio and newer message fields add their own overhead in real requests, and this tool does not model that. Treat the total as a lower-bound estimate.
